This project involves a review of the Commission’s current business processes. The appropriateness, efficiency and efficacy of the current processes are the focus and identifying areas that need improvement and suggesting ways of improvement are the required outcomes.

The Commission calculates States’ fiscal capacities on which it bases its recommendations. To do this, its data collection and calculation system (‘the data management system’) is a vital part of its business processes. The review needs to evaluate whether there are better ways of collecting, inputting, manipulating and analysing data, including whether these can be better integrated; and whether the Commission’s current in-house built calculation system is the best way of meeting the Commission’s data repository, calculation, analysis and reporting requirements.

Advice was sought by DLA Piper on behalf of the Auditing and Assurance Standards Board (AUASB) in relation to communication of Key Audit Matters.  AUASB standard setters sought clarification on the definition of a 'listed entity' under the Australian Accounting Standards and the requirement for auditors to communicate key audit matters (KAMs) during audits of financial reports under the Corporations Act.  DLA were instructed to determine by way of examination whether certain proposed amendments to ASA 701 which modify the scope of the requirement to communicate KAMs, are consistent with the equivalent international accounting standard, ISA 701 - and are therefore either 'ISA consistent' or 'ISA Plus' but not 'ISA negative'.  This legal advice is pertinent to the way the standards are interpreted and applied and vital to the integrity of communicating KAMs.
